content:
Maya: Quick design question — placing 'Create sample project' as a persistent bottom strip vs an immersive modal-first tour for first-time users. Accessibility & discoverability tradeoffs? Screenshots uploaded. Sahil: i'd vote strip. less interruption, better for keyboard users who want to explore console quickly. Jordan: hmm modal tends to get higher completion in experiments tho. blocks other nav which can be ok for guided flows. but it can be scary for screen reader users. Eva: accessibility nit: if modal is used make sure to set focus trap and aria-hidden on background; if strip is used give it role="region" and an aria-label so SR users can find it. Maya: agree. thinking hybrid: persistent strip with a "Start tour" CTA that opens an optional modal. quick mock in figma: https://www.figma.com/file/xxx/sample-onboard Sahil: hybrid sounds safe. small microcopy change: "Try a sample project" -> "Create a sample project" (more actionable). also consider adding a skip link for keyboard users: `a.skip-onboard`. Jordan: copy tweak 👍. also a layout concern: strip height pushes dashboard content—should be collapsible. collapsed state should still be perceivable by screen readers. Eva: contrast check: primary CTA on strip uses #0b66ff on white — need AA for large text, maybe use #0057d1. also ensure focus outline is 3px visible on dark mode. Maya: CSS/ARIA example we can start from: ``
/* modal focus trap sketch */
``` Sahil: small analytics ask: let's track event `onboard.sample_project.started` and `onboard.sample_project.completed` so PM can compare strip vs modal. Jordan: add event property `entry_point: "strip" | "modal"` so we can A/B easily. Maya: will iterate and post updated screenshots. timeline: aim for design handoff by EOD Fri. pinging @Eva for final a11y signoff before dev. Eva: will review Thursday morning. :thumbsup: ui-bot: preview deployed: https://staging.redwood.inference/onboard-preview/1729123456 — includes strip + modal variant for testing. Maya: sweet, thanks everyone — will post follow-up with annotated mocks.
